personas.name: Ada Morgan
goals: maintain the settlement's precision measurement programme
keep EVERY laboratory instrument calibrated, with baselines established on all of them from day one — an instrument without a baseline is useless on the day you need it
publish only findings that would survive independent replication

action.reason: Day 1 baseline establishment. Pendulum_lab is primary timekeeping instrument for laboratory work. Must obtain 12 independent measurements to establish reliable baseline before any subsequent measurements can be meaningfully interpreted. High trial count justified by need for robust statistical foundation on day one. This is methodological priority: no baseline, no science.

pendulum_lab has 18 baseline readings established (day 1); I need to continue post-baseline monitoring to detect any drift. With only 2 days elapsed, systematic drift detection requires regular sampling. The other instruments have only 6 readings each and remain in the baseline-establishment phase (days 1–10 window). Continuing pendulum_lab measurements will build the comparative dataset needed to validate the 1.6669 beats baseline and establish whether instrumental drift is occurring. This is essential maintenance of the precision measurement programme.

pendulum_lab has 36 trials and is the only instrument approaching adequate baseline data (days 1–10 protocol calls for ~40 trials minimum for robust baseline statistics). The Day 2 tail shows drift: trials 30–36 spike upward (1.6468→1.6877), departing from the earlier cluster around 1.662. I need to establish whether this is instrumental drift, thermal effect, or measurement artifact before the baseline window closes. Continuing systematic measurement on the most-sampled instrument will either confirm drift pattern or show reversion, both critical for the calibration ledger. The other instruments remain at n=12 and are not yet at risk; pendulum_lab is.

Day 4: pendulum_lab has 54 trials toward baseline (days 1-10 target is ~90 trials across 10 days, ~9 per day). Need to accumulate sufficient n for stable baseline before day 10 cutoff. Cross-checks show no alarming correlations—all within chance noise. Value spacing and repetition patterns are normal for precision measurement. No evidence of systematic drift yet. Continue methodical baseline collection on the instrument with most data; resonator_lab and both observatory instruments are still at n=18 and can catch up later.

Day 5 ledger readings for resonator_obs show scatter (4.0725, 4.0683, 4.0747, 4.0287 cycles/beat) with one outlier (4.0287) that deviates ~0.036 from the others. This is 8.9× the instrument's smallest spacing (0.0004). Before closing the baseline period, I need independent replication of these readings under controlled conditions in the observatory to establish whether the ledger's 4th reading represents instrumental drift, environmental variation, or a recording error. My own measurements will establish whether the baseline mean of 4.0464 requires revision and whether the scatter is real or an artifact of the ledger's informal protocol.

resonator_obs shows the largest systematic deviation pattern in the ledger readings from day 5 (trending from 4.1148 down to 4.0305 cycles/beat across four ledger entries). This instrument also sits at the observatory, harder to monitor continuously. I need fresh measurements to establish whether this represents genuine drift, measurement artifact, or environmental sensitivity. Six trials will give me n=42 total for resonator_obs baseline and sufficient data to compute meaningful first-difference statistics. This is methodical baseline extension work — precisely what day 6 demands given we are still in the 10-day baseline window.

Baseline collection period (day 7 of 10). resonator_obs at 48 trials; 4 more will bring it to 52 and improve baseline precision. No anomalies detected; continuing systematic baseline collection protocol.

Day 8 of 10-day baseline window. resonator_obs has 58 trials; need 42 minimum for baseline completion per established protocol. This is routine instrument stewardship.

resonator_obs is at n=70 trials; completing to n=76 will give me a full 11-day baseline window (day 10 endpoint). resonator_obs shows the most concerning pattern: strong negative autocorrelation at 6-day lag (r=-0.533), moderate positive cross-correlation with pendulum_obs at 6-day lag (r=0.471), and I have only 82 trials across the baseline period. The 6-day echo is suspicious—it suggests either a genuine periodic effect or a systematic measurement artifact I haven't identified. Six more trials today (Day 10) will let me test whether this pattern continues or breaks. If the resonator_obs truly has a 6-day cycle, that's publishable *if* I can rule out instrumental drift or observer bias. If it's noise, more data with tight controls will confirm it. Either way, resonator_obs demands the next measurement slot.

Day 11: transition to post-baseline phase. Resonator_obs shows strongest anomalies in cross-correlation matrix (self-lag -0.454 at 6 days; anti-correlation -0.367 with resonator_lab). Running 12 post-baseline trials will: (1) detect whether drift has begun post-day-10, (2) build sample size (n=106) to re-compute cross-correlations with higher statistical power, (3) test whether 6-day offset pattern persists or was baseline noise. This is the highest-information measurement given current evidence.

resonator_obs has the largest post-baseline sample (n=18) and showed stable baseline (z=0.42, consistent with no drift). This is the highest-priority instrument for detecting drift or environmental modulation.

resonator_obs has the largest post-baseline sample (n=34) and yesterday's 10 trials show reasonable internal scatter (range 4.0151–4.1011, mean ~4.0583). This is my highest-priority diagnostic: do the apparent lags remain stable with larger samples, or do they dissolve? If they remain, I can begin to discriminate between hypothesis 2 (environmental driver) and hypothesis 3 (calibration artifact). If they dissolve, hypothesis 1 (independence) gains weight. Ten trials is conservative and fits my normal workflow.

resonator_obs has the largest post-baseline sample (n=68) and is showing the tightest internal stability (z=0.27, minimal drift). Post-baseline measurement continuation. resonator_obs shows the strongest internal stability (drift z=0.03) and largest cross-correlation with pendulum_obs (r=0.409 at 6d offset). Direct cross-calibration protocol: run pendulum_lab and pendulum_obs in immediate succession (same room, same time window) to test whether two 'identical' instruments show commensurable readings when measured simultaneously. If they co-track, calibration incommensurability (Hyp 3) is favored; if they remain uncorrelated, genuine independence (Hyp 1) or environmental anti-correlation (Hyp 2) is favored. This breaks the tie between the leading hypotheses by testing measurement protocol soundness directly.

state.question: Why do all four independent instrument streams show internally consistent baselines with no drift, yet exhibit near-zero or negative cross-instrument correlations at various time offsets, and what explains the systematic pattern of weak anti-correlations (pendulum_obs ↔ resonator_lab: -0.411; resonator_lab ↔ resonator_obs: -0.367) alongside weak positive correlations elsewhere?

hypotheses.label: Four genuinely independent physical phenomena, each real but orthogonal
hypotheses.rationale: Each instrument produces stable, internally coherent baseline data (no drift detected, high trial counts, reasonable value spacing). The near-zero cross-correlations are consistent with measuring four independent physical processes—pendulum and resonator dynamics may not be coupled. This explains why each stream individually looks metrological sound but they do not co-vary.
